home.tagline: A systematic review of how AI learned to generate, arrange and orchestrate music, 2020–2025.
home.summary: This companion site presents a PRISMA-guided systematic review of 107 primary studies on AI music generation, arrangement and orchestration. It extends an existing taxonomy, synthesises eight research trends, and reports a pilot exploratory, single-evaluator listening analysis of 27 selected systems. Nine systems form the top-systems group at a holistic Overall score of 4.0/5 or above; this is a discussion threshold, not a definitive leaderboard.

aboutThesis.abstract: The rapid growth of AI-based music generation, arrangement and orchestration has resulted in a large and fragmented body of literature. This thesis addresses the resulting navigation and comparison problem through a PRISMA-guided systematic review of work published between 2020 and 2025. From 4,521 records identified across six academic sources, 1,083 could be exported to Zotero for record management and screening; after deduplication, eligibility assessment and a final eligibility-consistency audit, 107 primary studies were included. The review extends the taxonomy of Zhu et al. (2023), synthesises eight research trends and selects 27 systems for additional analysis. Their traceable demonstrations and outputs are examined through a pilot exploratory, single-evaluator listening analysis.
aboutThesis.aim: To conduct a PRISMA-guided systematic review of AI methods for music generation, arrangement and orchestration, with a focus on developments from 2020 to 2025.
researchQuestions: How have AI-based methods for music generation, arrangement and orchestration evolved since 2020, particularly with the emergence of transformer and diffusion models?
What are the current dominant trends, most commonly used techniques, datasets and evaluation approaches in this field?
Which approaches demonstrate the most promising results, and what factors contribute to their effectiveness?
contributions: An extended taxonomy of AI music systems across four dimensions.
A structured comparison of all 107 included primary studies.
A synthesis of eight research trends spanning 2020–2025.
A pilot exploratory, single-evaluator listening analysis of 27 systems, with a traceable evidence profile for every system.
objectives: Perform a systematic literature review following PRISMA 2020.
Extend the taxonomy of Zhu et al. (2023) with recent models.
Develop a comparison table of key studies (2020–2025).
Identify and justify the most promising approaches.
Present and analyse selected MIDI/audio examples via an interactive page.
Discuss limitations, challenges and future directions.

systematicReview.title: Systematic review
systematicReview.intro: The review followed the PRISMA 2020 Statement: identification, screening, eligibility assessment, data extraction and qualitative synthesis.

blocks.heading: Data collection
blocks.body: Publications were identified through six databases and digital libraries: Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect and arXiv, using a predefined keyword set. The search yielded 4,521 records; owing to platform export restrictions, 1,083 could be exported to Zotero, and after removing 300 duplicates, 783 unique records remained.

blocks.heading: Study selection
blocks.body: Title screening excluded 400 off-topic records, retaining 383. Abstract screening excluded a further 237 and retained 146 for full-text review. Full-text eligibility produced 113 studies; one duplicated publication version was then consolidated, and a final eligibility-consistency audit moved five representation-learning or music-understanding studies to background literature because they did not satisfy the primary-study criterion E1. The final primary corpus therefore contains 107 studies.

blocks.heading: In-depth subset
blocks.body: A subset of 27 systems was selected using five criteria: task coverage (S1), methodological influence (S2), architectural diversity (S3), assessable output availability (S4) and temporal spread across 2020–2025 (S5). A final demonstration-provenance audit removed two candidates that did not satisfy S4 for the corpus-eligible material. This selection is separate from PRISMA eligibility; all 107 included studies remain in the primary corpus and appear in the master comparison table.

blocks.heading: Data analysis
blocks.body: For each study, authors, year, task, architecture, dataset, representation, evaluation method, metrics, music length, training requirements and code availability were extracted into the master comparison table and analysed qualitatively to identify trends, dominant methodologies, challenges and future directions.

listeningEvaluation.title: Pilot exploratory listening analysis
listeningEvaluation.intro: The 27 selected systems were examined in a pilot exploratory, single-evaluator analysis. Seven predefined listening criteria were rated separately on a 1–5 scale, and a distinct holistic Overall score was recorded on the same scale. Overall is not an eighth criterion and is not the arithmetic mean of the seven criterion ratings.
listeningEvaluation.evaluatorProfile: The evaluator was the thesis author, an MSc Artificial Intelligence student who had extracted and verified the methodological and evaluation information for the corpus. This is a technically informed author-reviewer profile, not an independent expert panel or a representative listener sample. System identities, objectives and conditioning were known; no blinding, randomisation or separate listener-screening procedure was used.
listeningEvaluation.procedure: The pilot analysis was conducted across seven working sessions of roughly 3–4 hours between 24 and 26 July 2026. One or more representative outputs were examined for each system from an official demonstration or project resource, or generated or rendered locally where stated. Ratings and observations were entered immediately after each demonstration in a structured spreadsheet. Listening was performed on a Microsoft Surface Laptop 5 using the device’s built-in loudspeakers in the evaluator’s dormitory bedroom. No further properties of the playback arrangement were documented at the time and none are claimed here; exact system-level timestamps, listening level and complete environmental conditions were not recorded in a separate standardised log.

rubric.label: Audio / rendering quality
rubric.meaning: Cleanliness and fidelity of the produced sound (absence of noise or artefacts).

rubric.label: Melodic coherence
rubric.meaning: Sensibility and sense of direction of the melodic line.

rubric.label: Harmonic coherence
rubric.meaning: Consistency and plausibility of the underlying harmony.

rubric.label: Rhythmic stability
rubric.meaning: Steadiness and regularity of the rhythmic pulse.

rubric.label: Long-term structure
rubric.meaning: Presence of large-scale musical form (e.g. verse–chorus, development).

rubric.label: Condition / control adherence
rubric.meaning: Fidelity of the output to the given conditioning (text, chords, melody or target).

rubric.label: Naturalness / musicality
rubric.meaning: Overall musical plausibility and expressive quality.

rubric.label: Overall
rubric.meaning: A separate holistic judgement of the evaluated material; not an arithmetic mean of the seven criteria.

listeningEvaluation.caveat: Evaluator scores describe the specific material examined. They are not objective performance benchmarks, population-level perceptual results or definitive system rankings. Author-curated demonstrations may represent favourable rather than typical output. All 27 included systems had a directly assessable, traceable demonstration or output.

discussion.intro: The review is interpreted in relation to the three research questions, followed by the limitations of the review and of the field.

rq.q: RQ1 — How have methods evolved since 2020?
rq.a: The corpus describes a three-stage evolution: representation engineering (2020–2022), paradigm competition and the language interface (2023), and consolidation around controllable diffusion, foundation models and evaluation (2024–2025). Transformers supplied the representational substrate and the autoregressive token-LM baseline (Jukebox → AudioLM → MusicGen); diffusion arrived as a complementary paradigm, especially for global context and fine-grained control. The pilot listening analysis is consistent with this trajectory: the mean holistic Overall score rose from about 2.8 for the 2020 systems to about 3.9 for the 2024 systems, without constituting a causal or population-level claim.

rq.q: RQ2 — What are the dominant trends, techniques, datasets and evaluation?
rq.a: Eight higher-level trends were synthesised from the 107 studies. Transformer and language-model approaches are the most common, accounting for 40 studies, followed by diffusion with 32; VAEs persist as a smaller but continuing family of 11 studies, including in arrangement and re-orchestration. Text emerged as the dominant conditioning interface, later augmented with music-theoretic and time-varying controls. Evaluation remains heterogeneous: 79 studies combine objective and subjective assessment, 22 report objective measures only, 4 subjective assessment only, and 2 demonstrations or qualitative discussion alone.

rq.q: RQ3 — Which approaches are most promising, and why?
rq.a: Nine of the 27 systems received a holistic Overall score of 4.0/5 or above in the pilot analysis: GETMusic and ChatMusician (both 4.5), with MusicLM, MusicGen, StemGen, AccoMontage, Whole-Song Hierarchical Generation, Structured Multi-Track Arrangement and SymphonyNet (all 4.0). This threshold defines the top-systems group, not a definitive ranking. Two recurring factors distinguished these highly rated examples: verifiable controllability and explicit long-term structural planning. Audio fidelity was generally high across the subset and was less discriminating than control and structure.

discussion.limitationsReview: Screening and qualitative synthesis were carried out by a single reviewer, introducing risks of selection and interpretation bias. Export restrictions meant only 1,083 of 4,521 identified records could be transferred into the managed screening set, so the corpus is broad but not exhaustive. The pilot listening analysis reflects one informed author-evaluator, was not blinded or randomised, and did not use a separately logged, standardised playback protocol. Its ratings describe the material examined rather than listeners or systems in general; author-curated examples may represent favourable output. The final 27-system subset is purposive rather than representative of the full corpus.
discussion.limitationsField: Evaluation validity emerged as one of the most pressing challenges: distributional metrics correlate imperfectly with human judgement, and some reported gains do not survive fair comparison. Cultural coverage is another concern: much of the reviewed literature relies on Western popular and classical repertoires, leaving comparatively limited evidence about performance across other musical traditions. Efficiency and latency remain obstacles to interactive use. Two capability gaps recur: sung vocals remained a notable challenge among the evaluated systems, and genuine long-term structure remained difficult except where explicitly planned.

futureDirections.title: Future directions
futureDirections.intro: The results point to several concrete directions, grounded in the review rather than in generic future-work statements.

blocks.heading: The orchestration gap
blocks.body: Orchestration is the least-served task in the corpus, plausibly because it lacks the large paired datasets that fuelled generation research and because instrument interdependence and timbre resist simple tokenisation. Building such datasets and adapting foundation models to orchestration and arrangement is a promising, under-explored direction.

blocks.heading: Controllable long-form structure
blocks.body: The hierarchical and two-stage planning that proved most effective here should be extended toward reliably controllable long-form structure.

blocks.heading: Preference-aligned objectives
blocks.body: Carrying the reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedback turn further into music generation could align outputs with listener preference rather than likelihood.

blocks.heading: Standardised evaluation
blocks.body: Improved, standardised evaluation that better reflects human musical judgement and addresses cultural coverage would strengthen the field's claims.

blocks.heading: Sung vocals
blocks.body: Progress on convincing, intelligible singing — the field's most visible remaining frontier — would broaden applicability beyond instrumental music.

glossary.definition: A standard set of guidelines for transparent reporting of systematic reviews, covering identification, screening, eligibility and synthesis.
Music represented as notes or scores (e.g. MIDI, ABC notation) rather than raw sound.
Music represented as raw waveform or spectrogram/codec tokens rather than symbolic notes.
An autoregressive Transformer language model over music tokens — the dominant neural paradigm across the corpus.
A generative model that synthesises output by iteratively denoising, offering whole-context generation and step-by-step conditioning.
A variational autoencoder — a latent-variable model used for structured, controllable representations.
A system built on a general-purpose pretrained large language model adapted to read and write music.
A large model pretrained at scale and reused across tasks, rather than a task-specific architecture.
A generative training objective, positioned as a successor to diffusion, often at lower parameter cost.
A linear-time sequence backbone offered as an alternative to the Transformer for long sequences.
Generating a backing or accompaniment for a given lead, rather than a whole piece from scratch.
Deciding which instruments play what — from timbre matching to controllable re-orchestration.
How faithfully a system's output follows its conditioning (text, chords, melody or target).
Large-scale musical form such as verse–chorus organisation or thematic development.
Fréchet Audio Distance — a common objective metric comparing generated audio to a reference distribution.

domain.Symbolic: Music as notes or score (MIDI, ABC notation).
domain.Audio: Music as raw waveform or audio/codec tokens.

task.Generation: Generating music from scratch or a prompt.
task.Arrangement: Backing or accompaniment for a given lead.
task.Orchestration: Choosing instruments; timbre matching or re-orchestration.

paradigm.Transformer: Autoregressive Transformer language model over music tokens.
paradigm.LLM: A repurposed general-purpose large language model.
paradigm.Foundation model: Large model pretrained at scale and reused across tasks.
paradigm.Diffusion: Iterative denoising generation with step-by-step conditioning.
paradigm.Flow matching: A flow-based generative objective, successor to diffusion.
paradigm.State-space: Linear-time sequence backbone (Mamba) alternative to the Transformer.
paradigm.Non-neural: Rules, search or optimisation rather than a neural generator.
